definition: Running an AI system's actions (such as code execution) in an isolated environment to contain potential harm or unintended side effects.
details: Sandboxing is a critical safety measure for agentic systems that can execute code or take real-world actions, limiting the blast radius of mistakes, bugs, or malicious inputs.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. In plain words: Running an AI system's actions (such as code execution) in an isolated environment to contain potential harm or unintended side effects. Here is how it actually plays out: Sandboxing is a critical safety measure for agentic systems that can execute code or take real-world actions, limiting the blast radius of mistakes, bugs, or malicious inputs. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” That deliberate caution is Sandboxing.
